contract.definition: Publisher-assigned application number for an IP application, unique only within a given right type; it must be read together with the right type and is not a company registration number.

The kind of intellectual property right the application is for (e.g. patent), as published by IP Australia. It scopes the application number, so the pair (right type, application number) identifies the application; it is not a statement about the party or the company.

Australian Business Number supplied for an IP application party, sparsely populated and unvalidated in this source. It is an identifier only and must not be used to infer legal form, company status or a link to a business entity.

Start of the validity period of a party's recorded role episode on a specific IP application, as published (ISO-8601 timestamp with Z suffix). It is a party-activity validity date only: it is not a company incorporation or founding date, not an IP right grant or expiry date, and not evidence that the right is enforceable. It must be read with the party, application and role it qualifies.

End of the validity period of a party's recorded role episode on a specific IP application, as published (ISO-8601 timestamp with Z suffix); blank where the episode is open-ended. It is a party-activity validity date only: it is not a company dissolution date, not an IP right expiry date, and not evidence that the right is no longer enforceable.

Publisher flag stating whether the party's recorded role episode on the IP application is current in the source extract. It refers to the party record only; it is not a statement that the IP right is in force, enforceable or granted, and it is not a company status. It is not derivable from the validity dates.

Country code as supplied in the party's address on an IP application record, lower-cased and unnormalised (e.g. 'us', 'hk', 'in', 'il'). It is a party address field only; it is not a statement of the party's legal jurisdiction, nationality or legal form.

Postal code as supplied in the party's address on an IP application record, kept as raw text because formats are mixed and not normalised (e.g. '15666', '110044', '30024', 't6b 3n9'). It is a party address field only and is not a statement of the party's legal jurisdiction or of a business establishment location.

State or territory code as supplied in the party's address on an IP application record, lower-cased and unnormalised (e.g. 'vic', 'qld', 'nsw', 'wa'). It is a party address field only; it is not a statement of the party's legal jurisdiction, incorporation place or business operating location, and it must not be mapped onto the business subject's address.state enum without normalisation.

Publisher-assigned identifier for a party (organisation or individual) recorded on an IP application. It identifies the party across applications but is not a company registration number, ACN or ABN, and does not imply legal form or company status.

Publisher-supplied flag indicating whether the party is recorded as a founding party on the IP application record. It is a supplied party attribute flag only: it is not evidence of company incorporation, not a founding date, and not a statement of legal form or company status. Because the flag is published against a specific role episode (an agent row can carry it), it must be read with the party role and role category as well as the party and application.

Whether the IP application party is recorded by the publisher as an organisation or an individual. This is a party classification only; it is not a legal form, not a company status, and never implies sole trader.

Party name as published for an IP application party, lower-cased and unnormalised free text. It is a label only, not a unique identifier, and must not be used to join or deduplicate parties or to infer legal form.

The publisher's specific role label for the party on the IP application (e.g. patentee, applicant, agent, opponent_agent). 'other' denotes a publisher role label outside the enumerated subset and is not a missing-value signal; 'unknown' is reserved for a blank source value. It is a distinct dimension from the role category and must not be collapsed with it; an agent role is not evidence of ownership of the right.

The publisher's broad category of the capacity in which a party is recorded on an IP application (e.g. applicant, applicant_agent, opposition_agent, mortgagee). 'other' denotes a publisher category outside the enumerated subset (e.g. licensee) and is not a missing-value signal; 'unknown' is reserved for a blank source value. It is a role classification on the party-application involvement, not evidence of ownership of the right, not a legal form, and not a statement that the IP right is enforceable.
